name: Suzhou Ancient City Streets: Six Word Pairs
description:
Method replication: participants rate 20 street views from Suzhou's ancient city on six word pairs (beautiful–ugly, neat–messy, vibrant–depressing, safe–dangerous, characteristic–nondescript, wide–crowded), each on five levels from 1 (very negative word) through 3 (average) to 5 (very positive word); the images are not the paper's stimuli (53 newly fetched Baidu street views inside the moat, four directions at 20° upward pitch as in the paper).

Original study: Xu, Wang, Zuo & Han (2024), Journal of Urban Planning and Development 150(4), 05024036. Baidu panoramic static images (1,024 × 512, pitch 20°, headings 0/90/180/270°) at 2,937 points 50 m apart in Suzhou's ancient city were stitched into 2,936 panoramas. 35 volunteers (25 from across China, 10 local residents; mean age 32) rated 800 of them on the six pairs on five levels with a human–machine adversarial scoring tool; a random forest scored the rest, and the scores were combined with space syntax, POI and Weibo data to rank streets for improvement.

Differences from the original study: (1) the four views are shown as a 2 × 2 grid rather than one stitched strip, so they stay readable on phones; (2) 20 random images per participant and no machine pre-scores; (3) answers use numbered buttons with the end words shown under each pair.
author: Xu, Wang, Zuo & Han
